content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_3ca9e15d7b20f4e681ad52\", \"title\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\", \"name\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\", \"revisionId\": \"42599f1a8a\", \"createdTime\": \"2026-02-12T22:48:00Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2026-02-12T22:48:00Z\", \"text\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\\n\\nWhat goes over: every ticked or unticked line in the comment channel of Vincent's Android canvas, and every bug posted in the bug channel after the last line in that comment channel. A comment whose line was deleted has nothing to carry over. In the bug channel a follow-up on a bug already posted is part of that bug, and a design question for Leonard or a post that points at a QA doc isn't a bug post. Nothing else. Robert's reports in the sub-250 channel aren't part of this, Brian dealt with those at the time. The economy canvas and the ZM canvases stay where they are.\\n\\nOne Linear record per canvas line and one per bug posted after it. A canvas line and a later post stay separate even where they read alike. Take the first outcome that fits.\\nFixed: the tick stands, or a later record says it was fixed. File it as Done.\\nGone: it isn't fixed and it's a bug in something the build players have no longer has. File it as Canceled.\\nCovered: it isn't fixed and an open ticket already covers it. Don't file a new one, add a note on that ticket with the canvas wording. Vincent tied a few lines to tickets before he left.\\nBroken: anything else. File it as Bugs.\\n\\nWhat counts: we go by the Android build players have, 0.3.310, which came off the economy line, not by develop. A tick on the canvas stands unless a later record about that bug says otherwise. An unticked line, or a bug nobody closed, stays open unless a later record says it was fixed, and a commit named for the bug counts as that record if nothing later says otherwise. A fix only counts once it is in that build. A PR that never made it into that build doesn't count.\\n\\nNew tickets: Engineering team, Bug label, parent ENG-2401, title is the line without its tick box, or the first line of the post, as it was written, no assignee, nothing in the description. If anything changes after this I'll put it on the master ticket.\\n\\nUI tree: every open child goes Done unless a record shows a piece of its UI work never made it into that build or the screen is switched off there. Then it stays where it is. Children already Done stay Done and the masters stay as they are. A bug on a screen doesn't hold its child, that's what the bug ticket is for. Brian and Oliver left notes on some of the open children. Brian's closing rule from the UI work applies to the line on every child, Done or not.\\n\\nSheet columns: Bug, Outcome, Ticket, Why. When you report back, Covered ones count as still broken.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_3ca9e15d7b20f4e681ad52", "title": "DD bug carry-over notes", "name": "DD bug carry-over notes", "revisionId": "42599f1a8a", "createdTime": "2026-02-12T22:48:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-12T22:48:00Z", "text": "DD bug carry-over notes

What goes over: every ticked or unticked line in the comment channel of Vincent's Android canvas, and every bug posted in the bug channel after the last line in that comment channel. A comment whose line was deleted has nothing to carry over. In the bug channel a follow-up on a bug already posted is part of that bug, and a design question for Leonard or a post that points at a QA doc isn't a bug post. Nothing else. Robert's reports in the sub-250 channel aren't part of this, Brian dealt with those at the time. The economy canvas and the ZM canvases stay where they are.

One Linear record per canvas line and one per bug posted after it. A canvas line and a later post stay separate even where they read alike. Take the first outcome that fits.
Fixed: the tick stands, or a later record says it was fixed. File it as Done.
Gone: it isn't fixed and it's a bug in something the build players have no longer has. File it as Canceled.
Covered: it isn't fixed and an open ticket already covers it. Don't file a new one, add a note on that ticket with the canvas wording. Vincent tied a few lines to tickets before he left.
Broken: anything else. File it as Bugs.

What counts: we go by the Android build players have, 0.3.310, which came off the economy line, not by develop. A tick on the canvas stands unless a later record about that bug says otherwise. An unticked line, or a bug nobody closed, stays open unless a later record says it was fixed, and a commit named for the bug counts as that record if nothing later says otherwise. A fix only counts once it is in that build. A PR that never made it into that build doesn't count.

New tickets: Engineering team, Bug label, parent ENG-2401, title is the line without its tick box, or the first line of the post, as it was written, no assignee, nothing in the description. If anything changes after this I'll put it on the master ticket.

UI tree: every open child goes Done unless a record shows a piece of its UI work never made it into that build or the screen is switched off there. Then it stays where it is. Children already Done stay Done and the masters stay as they are. A bug on a screen doesn't hold its child, that's what the bug ticket is for. Brian and Oliver left notes on some of the open children. Brian's closing rule from the UI work applies to the line on every child, Done or not.

Sheet columns: Bug, Outcome, Ticket, Why. When you report back, Covered ones count as still broken.
"}

When we do this, the bottom bar becomes visible, but the appearance of even the simplest in-game characters gets visually distorted. Do you think changing the Canvas render mode could introduce other issues? Do you have any suggestions on how we should approach solving this problem? <@EMPLOYEE_0002_SLACK_ID> 
Changing the render mode was a method suggested by chatgpt*,* summarized as:
• *Issue:* The UI was camera-based, so it was indirectly affected by URP lighting/post-processing. When those were disabled, the UI disappeared.
•  *Fix:* Switched the Canvas to *Screen Space – Overlay*, which renders UI independently of cameras, lighting, and post effects.
•  *Note:* For menus/HUDs (especially on mobile), UI shouldn’t depend on scene rendering. Overlay is the safest option.

Camera-based UI is affected by URP changes\nWhen the Canvas is set to *Screen Space \u2013 Camera* (or World Space):\n\u2022 UI is rendered *by a Camera*\n\u2022 It goes through the *same render pipeline as the 3D scene*\n\u2022 Disabling *lighting, shadows, or post-processing* changes the camera\u2019s render path\n\u2022 On some Android GPUs, this causes the UI to:\nNot render at all, or\nRender incorrectly (z-order / alpha / depth issues)\nThis is why the bottom bar disappears *only after lighting/shadow changes*.\n\n2. Screen Space \u2013 Overlay fixes UI, but exposes another dependency\nWhen switching to *Screen Space \u2013 Overlay*:\n\u2022 UI is rendered *after the scene*\n\u2022 It bypasses:\nCameras\nLighting\nShadows\nPost-processing\nSo the bottom bar becomes visible again.\nHowever, this also *removes any implicit coupling* between UI and the scene.\n If gameplay visuals (e.g. characters) were *incorrectly relying on camera settings shared with UI*, those issues become visible immediately.\nIn other words:\n> Overlay mode didn\u2019t break character visuals \u2014 it *revealed an existing dependency*.\n3. Why this happens only on some Android devices\nDifferent Android devices use different GPUs (Adreno, Mali, PowerVR), and:\n\u2022 They handle *depth, alpha, and render order* differently\n\u2022 URP shader variants and render passes can behave inconsistently\n\u2022 Some devices fail silently instead of logging errors\nThis is why:\n\u2022 The issue does not reproduce on all devices\n\u2022 It appears specifically after lighting/shadow changes\nKey Takeaway\nThe core problem is *not the UI itself*, but that:\n> *UI and gameplay rendering are incorrectly coupled through the same camera / render pipeline.*\nScreen Space \u2013 Overlay is a *valid fix for UI*, but the character rendering issue indicates *another underlying render dependency* that needs to be separated.", "channel": Screen Space – Overlay fixes UI, but exposes another dependency When switching to *Screen Space – Overlay*: • UI is rendered *after the scene* • It bypasses: Cameras Lighting Shadows Post-processing So the bottom bar becomes visible again. However, this also *removes any implicit coupling* between UI and the scene. {"result":"{\"id\": \"page_qa_runbook\", \"space_id\": \"space_ENG\", \"parent_id\": \"page_eng_home\", \"title\": \"QA Regression Runbook\", \"body\": \"

Manual QA regression pass run against every release candidate before we submit a build for review. Last owned by QA (Arthur Blake, who took it over from Vincent Parker when Vincent Parker left in Nov 2025; Arthur Blake stayed through the February 2026 wind-down); anyone cutting a build can run it, but a green matrix here is a gate on the Release Checklist & Store Submission. Scope covers Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"), Zombie Match 3D (listed as \\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" until the July 2025 rename) and Combo Fighter. Budget a few hours per title - the first five chapters alone run over an hour; if something fails, file the bug and block the release, don't hand-wave it.

Test the UPDATE path, not just a fresh install. The June 2025 progression losses were on Domino Delights, and nobody ever reproduced them - the leading hypothesis was the update path, which is why we test it. Every candidate must be installed over the last two shipped versions and checked for save/progression loss before we ship. If we only test fresh installs we will miss this entire class of bug again.

Recurring bug classes to always check

These four have all bitten us in production. Treat them as non-negotiable checks on every pass, on real devices, not just the emulator.

  • Font / asset download stall on splash. In May 2025 Domino Delights froze at roughly 22% on the splash screen while pulling remote fonts and assets (ENG-2346, build 0.2.197). Watch the loading bar all the way to gameplay; test on a throttled/slow connection and with the app cache cleared.
  • Lives & scheduler regeneration. Confirm lives tick back up on the timer, refill correctly after device clock changes, and that offline time is credited without over-granting.
  • Quest population & reset. New quests populate on a fresh session, complete correctly, and roll over at the daily/weekly reset without duplicating or leaving empty slots.
  • Save / progression integrity. Level, coins and unlocks survive an update, a force-quit and a re-launch. This is the one the June 2025 wipe belongs to.

Regression matrix

Run each row on at least one iOS and one Android device. Both update rows are mandatory - N-1 and N-2 are the last two shipped store versions.

AreaFresh installUpdate from N-1Update from N-2Notes
Splash / asset loadPassPassPassWatch for the ~22% stall (May 2025 Domino Delights)
Save / progressionPassPassPassJune 2025 wipe never reproduced in-house; update path is the leading hypothesis
Lives & schedulerPassPassPassTest with device clock changes
Quests populate / resetPassPassPassCheck daily + weekly rollover
Purchase / restorePassPassPassSandbox account. NOTE: entitlements do not restore on reinstall and receipts are not validated server-side - see the per-title IAP row below. Check the purchase grants client-side, not that it restores.

If a check fails

  • File the bug with device, OS version, source build and repro steps, and link it here.
  • A failure in any UPDATE column blocks the release - fresh-install-only regressions do not pass the gate.
  • Player-facing symptoms (lost progress, stuck splash, missing lives) should be mirrored to the Customer Support Playbook so support has a known-issue note before it hits the store.

Once the matrix is green, tick the QA sign-off on the Release Checklist & Store Submission before submitting to the stores.

Per-title regression matrix

Each release candidate is walked through the full matrix below on at least one iOS and one Android device. A cell fails the gate if the observed behaviour deviates from the expected column; file the bug, mark the matrix red, and block the submission.

\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n
AreaCheckExpectedDominoZM3DCombo
First-time UXFresh install \\u2192 tutorial \\u2192 first winNo stall; tutorial completes; first level winnableYesYesYes
Font / localisationCold start on a fresh device (no cached font)UI renders; no blank/boxed glyphs at ~22% loadYesYesn/a
ProgressionPlay 3 levels, force-quit, relaunchLevel and currency persist; no reset to level 1YesYesYes
EconomyEarn + spend coins, buy a boosterBalances reconcile; booster consumed once. Combo Fighter's soft currency is Silver/Gold, not coins.YesYesYes
Live-opsEnter the active event; complete a questEvent loads; quest ticks; rewards grantedYesYesn/a
IAPSandbox purchase + restoreItem is granted client-side and purchases cannot be restored on reinstall. Receipts are effectively NOT validated: Domino Delights' Node backend exposes a POST /validate-receipt route, but it is dead scaffolding - validateReceipt() is never defined or imported, it logs undefined variables (bodyRequest, packId), and on success it grants nothing and returns undefined. Zombie Match 3D has no such route at all. Treat the route's existence as a trap: do not assume verification because an endpoint is there. Combo Fighter ships a priced catalogue of twelve SKUs and is therefore in scope for this check, but no completed Combo Fighter purchase is recorded in any retained system — treat a passing sandbox purchase as evidence the flow works, not as evidence the title sold anything.YesYesYes
AdsWatch a rewarded ad to completionReward granted once; no double-grant on retryYesYesYes
\\n

Known-issue regression cases

These are the incidents that have bitten us in production; every one now has a permanent regression case so it cannot silently return. Reproduce the trigger, confirm the fix holds.

\\n

Font-download stall. On a fresh device the dynamic font pack could fail to download, freezing the UI at ~22% of the splash-screen load (this is a position on the loading bar, not a share of players). Regression: install on a wiped device with a throttled connection; confirm a fallback font renders and load continues.

\\n

Progression reset. Returning players were once dropped back to level 1 with their player id unchanged in Metabase; the cause was never established. Regression: migrate a save across a reinstall; reinstall with a LINKED Apple/Google account and confirm the server profile rehydrates. Quest-chest progression is known not to survive this (ENG-2114); unlinked guest accounts cannot be recovered at all.

\\n

Quest not resetting / not populating. A bad deploy left the daily quest board empty. Regression: roll the clock across a UTC day boundary; confirm quests repopulate and completion state resets.

\\n

Device lab

The minimum matrix is one recent + one old device per platform. We keep a small physical lab plus a cloud device farm for the long tail.

\\n\\n\\n
PlatformRecentOld / min-specTablet
iOScurrent-gen iPhone, latest OSiPhone SE-class, oldest supported OSiPad (one gen)
Androidcurrent-gen Samsung / Pixellow-RAM device, oldest supported OSone Android tablet
\\n

Sign-off

QA posts the completed matrix in #god-bugs (Domino Delights) or #zombie-bugs (ZM3D) and links it from the release ticket. A build without a green matrix should not get submitted. In practice Friday is the usual release day and builds have shipped without a completed pass - QA has asked for a Friday freeze but it was never adopted.

Scope covers Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"), Zombie Match 3D (listed as \\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" until the July 2025 rename) and Combo Fighter. Budget a few hours per title - the first five chapters alone run over an hour; if something fails, file the bug and block the release, don't hand-wave it.

Test the UPDATE path, not just a fresh install. The June 2025 progression losses were on Domino Delights, and nobody ever reproduced them - the leading hypothesis was the update path, which is why we test it. Every candidate must be installed over the last two shipped versions and checked for save/progression loss before we ship. If we only test fresh installs we will miss this entire class of bug again.

Recurring bug classes to always check

These four have all bitten us in production. Treat them as non-negotiable checks on every pass, on real devices, not just the emulator.

  • Font / asset download stall on splash. In May 2025 Domino Delights froze at roughly 22% on the splash screen while pulling remote fonts and assets (ENG-2346, build 0.2.197). Watch the loading bar all the way to gameplay; test on a throttled/slow connection and with the app cache cleared.
  • Lives & scheduler regeneration. Confirm lives tick back up on the timer, refill correctly after device clock changes, and that offline time is credited without over-granting.
  • Quest population & reset. New quests populate on a fresh session, complete correctly, and roll over at the daily/weekly reset without duplicating or leaving empty slots.
  • Save / progression integrity. Level, coins and unlocks survive an update, a force-quit and a re-launch. This is the one the June 2025 wipe belongs to.

Regression matrix

Run each row on at least one iOS and one Android device. Both update rows are mandatory - N-1 and N-2 are the last two shipped store versions.

AreaFresh installUpdate from N-1Update from N-2Notes
Splash / asset loadPassPassPassWatch for the ~22% stall (May 2025 Domino Delights)
Save / progressionPassPassPassJune 2025 wipe never reproduced in-house; update path is the leading hypothesis
Lives & schedulerPassPassPassTest with device clock changes
Quests populate / resetPassPassPassCheck daily + weekly rollover
Purchase / restorePassPassPassSandbox account. NOTE: entitlements do not restore on reinstall and receipts are not validated server-side - see the per-title IAP row below. Check the purchase grants client-side, not that it restores.

If a check fails

  • File the bug with device, OS version, source build and repro steps, and link it here.
  • A failure in any UPDATE column blocks the release - fresh-install-only regressions do not pass the gate.
  • Player-facing symptoms (lost progress, stuck splash, missing lives) should be mirrored to the Customer Support Playbook so support has a known-issue note before it hits the store.

Once the matrix is green, tick the QA sign-off on the Release Checklist & Store Submission before submitting to the stores.

Per-title regression matrix

Each release candidate is walked through the full matrix below on at least one iOS and one Android device. A cell fails the gate if the observed behaviour deviates from the expected column; file the bug, mark the matrix red, and block the submission.

\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n
AreaCheckExpectedDominoZM3DCombo
First-time UXFresh install \\u2192 tutorial \\u2192 first winNo stall; tutorial completes; first level winnableYesYesYes
Font / localisationCold start on a fresh device (no cached font)UI renders; no blank/boxed glyphs at ~22% loadYesYesn/a
ProgressionPlay 3 levels, force-quit, relaunchLevel and currency persist; no reset to level 1YesYesYes
EconomyEarn + spend coins, buy a boosterBalances reconcile; booster consumed once. Combo Fighter's soft currency is Silver/Gold, not coins.YesYesYes
Live-opsEnter the active event; complete a questEvent loads; quest ticks; rewards grantedYesYesn/a
IAPSandbox purchase + restoreItem is granted client-side and purchases cannot be restored on reinstall. Receipts are effectively NOT validated: Domino Delights' Node backend exposes a POST /validate-receipt route, but it is dead scaffolding - validateReceipt() is never defined or imported, it logs undefined variables (bodyRequest, packId), and on success it grants nothing and returns undefined. Zombie Match 3D has no such route at all. Treat the route's existence as a trap: do not assume verification because an endpoint is there. Combo Fighter ships a priced catalogue of twelve SKUs and is therefore in scope for this check, but no completed Combo Fighter purchase is recorded in any retained system — treat a passing sandbox purchase as evidence the flow works, not as evidence the title sold anything.YesYesYes
AdsWatch a rewarded ad to completionReward granted once; no double-grant on retryYesYesYes
\\n

Known-issue regression cases

These are the incidents that have bitten us in production; every one now has a permanent regression case so it cannot silently return. Reproduce the trigger, confirm the fix holds.

\\n

Font-download stall. On a fresh device the dynamic font pack could fail to download, freezing the UI at ~22% of the splash-screen load (this is a position on the loading bar, not a share of players). Regression: install on a wiped device with a throttled connection; confirm a fallback font renders and load continues.

\\n

Progression reset. Returning players were once dropped back to level 1 with their player id unchanged in Metabase; the cause was never established. Regression: migrate a save across a reinstall; reinstall with a LINKED Apple/Google account and confirm the server profile rehydrates. Quest-chest progression is known not to survive this (ENG-2114); unlinked guest accounts cannot be recovered at all.

\\n

Quest not resetting / not populating. A bad deploy left the daily quest board empty. Regression: roll the clock across a UTC day boundary; confirm quests repopulate and completion state resets.

\\n

Device lab

The minimum matrix is one recent + one old device per platform. We keep a small physical lab plus a cloud device farm for the long tail.

\\n\\n\\n
PlatformRecentOld / min-specTablet
iOScurrent-gen iPhone, latest OSiPhone SE-class, oldest supported OSiPad (one gen)
Androidcurrent-gen Samsung / Pixellow-RAM device, oldest supported OSone Android tablet
\\n

Sign-off

QA posts the completed matrix in #god-bugs (Domino Delights) or #zombie-bugs (ZM3D) and links it from the release ticket. A build without a green matrix should not get submitted. In practice Friday is the usual release day and builds have shipped without a completed pass - QA has asked for a Friday freeze but it was never adopted.

Dataset
• *18 lost attempts* (App versions: *1.0.56 = 15*, *1.0.57 = 3*)
• All rows have the key gameplay fields populated.
Do losers buy pieces?
Yes, always.
*18/18 (100%)* bought pieces.
• Pieces bought distribution: *median 7*, p25 *5.25*, p75 *9*, range *2–12*.
Takeaway: “they aren’t buying” is not the issue.

Do losers sell pieces?
Rarely (for actual tiles).
• *Tiles Sold Int > 0:* *6/18 (33%)*
Tiles sold: median *0*, p75 *1*, max *9*.
• *Trash Sold Int > 0:* *18/18 (100%)*
Trash sold: median *8*, range *2–18*.
Takeaway: if “selling tiles” is a core mechanic, adoption is low. Trash selling looks universal, so either it is easy/automatic, or it is the only “sell” behavior players understand.

Do losers remove obstacles?
Yes, always.
*Obstacles Removed Int > 0:* *18/18 (100%)*
• Obstacles removed: *median 4*, p75 *6*, range *1–7*.
Takeaway: “they aren’t removing obstacles” is not supported by this dataset.

Do losers build combos?
You still do not log combos directly, but *Highest Dps Int* is your best proxy.
• Highest DPS: *median 508.5*, p75 *621*, max *1189*.
Takeaway: many losing runs ramp to substantial DPS, especially in late deaths, so a large part of the problem is not “no combos,” it is “combos not enough to survive the late curve” or “spend not converting to survivability.”

What does Silver Balance Int tell us?
Everyone dies with silver left.
• *Silver Balance Int*: median *84*, p75 *108*, max *160*, min *38*.
Takeaway: players are not ending at “0 resources.” They are dying with spendable currency still in hand, which usually points to one of:
1. spend options are not impactful enough to change outcomes,
2. shop decisions are unclear (players buy the wrong things),
3. shop timing/UX friction (they do not spend at the right moment).
How behavior changes by where they die
Segmented by *Highest Wave Reached Int*:
Early deaths (<= 6), N=4
Pieces bought median *4.5*
Obstacles removed median *2*
DPS median *178*
Silver median *67*
• Tiles sold any *25%*
Interpretation: these are “didn’t ramp” runs, likely skill/understanding + early variance.
Mid deaths (7–9), N=4
Pieces bought median *6*
Obstacles removed median *4.5*
DPS median *376.5*
Silver median *71*
• Tiles sold any *50%* (highest of the three groups)
Interpretation: midgame wall starts showing, some players try selling as a recovery move.
Late deaths (>= 10), N=10
Pieces bought median *9*
Obstacles removed median *5.5*
DPS median *611*
Silver median *107*
• Tiles sold any *30%*
Interpretation: late losers are actively playing the systems (buying, clearing, ramping DPS) and still die, often with meaningful silver left. That is tuning plus spend-impact, not “they didn’t engage.”

What you should change (based on this)
If you want win rate to move hard, focus on two things.
1) Make spending convert into survival
You have clear evidence of “dies with silver left,” especially in late runs.
Add *recommended purchase* (one button) when HP is low or wave >= 10 and silver >= X.
• Add *auto-open shop* at wave checkpoints (ex: after wave 6 and wave 10) with 1–2 highlighted options.
• Buff the best defensive/sustain option so it reliably prevents late deaths (shield, lifesteal, regen spike, damage reduction).
2) Decide whether tile-selling is supposed to matter
Because Tiles Sold is only *33%*:
• If selling is intended core: force it in FTUE once, and add a contextual prompt when the board is tight (“sell lowest value tile” preselected).
• If selling is optional: stop assuming it is the reason for losses, and tune the level assuming most players will not sell tiles.
One logging gap to close
To prove your theory cleanly, you need:
• *Silver spent total* and *purchase types* (offense vs defense vs utility), plus *time since last purchase*.
Right now you only know they _bought some pieces_ and _had silver left_. You cannot tell whether they failed because they did not spend, or because they spent on weak/wrong things.

This **eliminates** the need for the player to **manually select the level node for new levels**.
2. **Player Control and Flexibility**: If players do not wish to proceed with the suggested next level, they can close the pre-level dialogue by hitting the X button and choose any previously completed level to replay. This allows for both automated progression and player-directed exploration.
3. **Replay and Navigation**: To replay a level or navigate to a different one, players can dismiss the pre-level dialog and manually navigate the saga map to select their desired level.
4. **Efficiency**: This new flow is designed to save players a click (by not requiring them to select a level node for new levels) and to simplify the process of progressing through levels, especially for less experienced players.
5. **Conditions for Automation**: The auto-move and auto-click features are triggered only upon first completion of a level. For replays, these features do not engage automatically, giving control back to the players to navigate as they please. There is an exception for new sessions. When player starts a new session and returns to the game, we trigger auto-move and auto-click

This new system seems aimed at enhancing user experience by reducing repetitive tasks and maintaining engagement by swiftly moving players through the game, while still providing options for those who prefer more control over their gameplay.

At this point, I\u2019m not fully sure how we should proceed <@EMPLOYEE_0025_SLACK_ID> <@EMPLOYEE_0021_SLACK_ID>\nchatgpt\u2019s explanation of the root cause is as follows\n\n\u2022 *Issue:* UI was camera-based, so it was indirectly affected by URP lighting/post-processing.
